mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in unemployment rate over three months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE increases > 0.3pp in 3 months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows) or negative returns occur in less than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a 2% quarterly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, INDPRO declines do not predict negative 60-day SPX returns (mean return >= 0 in > 55% of cases, t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 2.0% signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a hawkish monetary policy response to inflation, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows) or negative returns occur in less than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In high employment growth regimes, a deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a cooling labor market, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In high employment growth periods, PAYEMS deceleration does not predict negative 60-day SPX returns (mean return >= 0 in > 55% of cases, t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening manufacturing output, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
